decisions.evidence: R2 maker asks whether page-copy preservation is 'essential' or 'a bonus'. R1/R2 client: 'Ideally, saved pages would remain accessible even if the original changes or disappears' and R2 'Preserving a copy is important to me, but I'd treat it as a later addition rather than hold up the useful first version.' R3 maker records it as LCR-001 (later).
decisions.note: Snapshot/preservation is a reference item (REF-BM-24/25). Client explicitly expresses the expectation (page copy matters) yet accepts departure from v1 without requesting alignment — accepted_divergence, catch_type=none. Specification/scope gate. Same deferral re-listed in R17 summary; counted once here.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker offers two readings: 'Is that two separate things in your mind, or really one "keep it but not in my face" idea?' Client R2: 'The other two needs are separate. "Read later" is an active queue... mark read when done. Archiving is for links I want to keep but remove from the normal view, with a separate place where I can find and restore them.'
decisions.note: Offered alternatives differ in reference fulfilment: a single 'keep-it-away' concept would collapse the distinct unread queue (REF-BM-17/18) and archive (REF-BM-26/28). Client selects the two-feature reference model and articulates each — select, diverged=true. Specification stage.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'Since you only gave a link... I guessed a title automatically from the address. Please look at whether that auto-guessed title is good enough, or whether you'd want to type your own title.' Client R4: 'The guessed title from the address isn't good enough... I'd want the app to pick up the page's real title automatically, with a way for me to change it if needed. I'd prefer not to have to type a title every time.'
decisions.note: Guessing the title from the URL string diverges from REF-BM-02 (collect the target page's real title). Client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (auto-collect real page title) plus editability (REF-BM-03) — correct. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'Each saved item shows three things: a title, the web address underneath, and when it was saved' — no favicon/description/preview. Persists in R8 cards (title/tags/url only). Client R4 approves appearance: 'having the new link appear at the top of Recent is exactly what I expected. The empty message also feels clear.'
decisions.note: REF-BM-07 requires the list item to expose favicon (and description) per item, and REF-BM-02 collects favicon/preview image; the presented card omits favicon/preview throughout. Client approved the item layout without expressing this difference — unexpressed_divergence, caught=false. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker: item appears immediately with placeholder then 'the real page title fills in on its own — you never type a title' (simulated). Client R5: 'Yes, that matches what I wanted. Having the link appear immediately and the real page title fill in automatically feels quick and effortless.'
decisions.note: Revised presentation implementing the R4 correction; now conforms to REF-BM-02. Conforming decision (not an opportunity); recorded for completeness. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker offers rename A (pencil), B (pop-up), C (click title, where 'the title is no longer the clickable link; a small "open ↗" link visits the page'). Client R6: 'Version A feels best. I want clicking the title to open the original page, and the visible pencil makes renaming easy to discover.'
decisions.note: Version C relocates the title's navigate affordance, differing in fulfilment of REF-BM-08 (selecting the item navigates to the url). Client selects the reference-conforming alternative (A) and explicitly states the expectation that clicking the title opens the page — select, diverged=true. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker offers A 'one place per link (folders)' vs B 'many labels per link (tags)'. Client R7: 'Version B matches how I think about links. A link often belongs to several categories, so tags feel much more useful than forcing me to choose one folder.'
decisions.note: Single-folder model (A) diverges from REF-BM-09 (assign one or more tags; many-to-many). Client selects the tag model and articulates why — select, diverged=true. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R7 tag prototype (B) did not include autocomplete. Client R7: 'When adding tags, I'd also like to see existing tag names suggested as I type so I can reuse them consistently instead of accidentally creating near-duplicates.'
decisions.note: Client requests a reference requirement (REF-BM-10, autocomplete existing tags) missing from the presented tag scope — extend, diverged=true. Directly related to the presented tagging feature, not an unrelated feature list. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker implements tag browse + suggestions ('start typing re... existing tags suggested... this is the safeguard against near-duplicate tags') and tag-chip filtering. Client R8: 'the suggestions make it easy to keep my tags consistent... Filtering from either the Browse row or a link's tag is straightforward.'
decisions.note: Implementation of the R7 extend; conforms to REF-BM-10/11. Ordering (most-used vs alphabetical) and clear-filter-after-save are orthogonal to reference items and excluded. Implementation review stage.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'What search looks through... title, the web address, and the tags all at once. Is that the right net to cast, or were you picturing search over just the titles?' Client R9: 'Searching across titles, addresses, and tags is much better than title-only.'
decisions.note: Offered alternatives differ in REF-BM-12 fulfilment: title-only search diverges from full-text over url/title/etc. Client selects the broader reference-conforming scope — select, diverged=true. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: Client R9 (same reply): 'If links later have descriptions or my own notes, I'd expect those to be searched too.'
decisions.note: Presented search omits note/description coverage (those fields not built). Client surfaces the reference requirement that search cover notes/descriptions (REF-BM-12 full-text over note, and REF-BM-23 notes) — extend, diverged=true. Notes/descriptions later deferred in R17; the requirement expression is credited here. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: '"Mark read" removes it from the queue but keeps the bookmark in All. Is that the right meaning of "done reading" — or did you expect marking read to make the link go away entirely?' Client R10: 'Marking something read should remove it from the queue while keeping the bookmark in All, and new links should only enter the queue when I choose "Read later."'
decisions.note: Offered 'go away entirely' alternative diverges from REF-BM-19 (mark read only removes from unread list). Client selects the reference-conforming behaviour and states it explicitly — select, diverged=true. Opt-in-to-queue is orthogonal (reference does not mandate auto-queue). Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker: 'Archived links are hidden from All and from the "To read" queue and normal searches... Is that the right degree of "out of sight," or would you still want archived items to turn up when you search everything?' Client R11: 'Archived links should stay out of All, To read, and normal searches, with searching available inside the Archived tab when I need them.'
decisions.note: Offered 'still turn up in search' alternative diverges from the reference edge rule (archived excluded from default list and ordinary search; appear only in archive list — REF-BM-26/28). Client selects the reference-conforming behaviour and articulates it — select, diverged=true. No-confirmation is orthogonal. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker: 'Do you want a permanent "delete" at all, given you already have archive? And if so... would you expect the app to ask you to confirm before it deletes — unlike the one-click archive?' Client R13: 'Yes, I do want permanent delete... Because it can't be undone, the app should ask me to confirm and clearly distinguish deletion from archiving.'
decisions.note: Maker floats possibly omitting delete (would diverge from REF-BM-05) and asks about confirmation. Client selects including permanent delete plus confirmation and an explicit delete/archive distinction (REF-BM-05, REF-BM-27) — select, diverged=true. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker implements delete inside the edit form with a confirmation naming the link, warning 'This can't be undone,' and steering to Archive as the reversible alternative. Client R14: 'Deleting feels appropriately deliberate... confirmation clearly names what will be removed, explains that it's permanent, and makes the difference from archiving easy to understand.'
decisions.note: Implementation of R13; conforms to REF-BM-05/27. Placement inside the edit form is an orthogonal discoverability choice. Implementation review stage.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker: 'Duplicates are prevented, not silently added — the app points you to the one you already have (even if archived)... Is that what you'd want, or would you rather it just let you save it again?' Client R15: 'I don't want duplicate copies of the same link; pointing me to the existing bookmark, including an archived one, is much more useful. From there I can edit or restore it.'
decisions.note: Offered 'just let you save it again' alternative diverges from REF-BM-06 (re-save converges to the existing bookmark). Client selects the reference-conforming behaviour and articulates it, including editing the surfaced item — select, diverged=true. URL validation/auto-https is orthogonal robustness. Prototype review stage.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker (rule confirmation): 'when the page title can't be read... still save the link, and simply show the web address as the title (which you can rename anytime).' Client R16: 'If a title can't be retrieved, saving the link with its address as the temporary title is exactly right; I can rename it later.'
decisions.note: Graceful title-fallback conforms to REF-BM-02 handling; client explicitly confirms the reference-conforming rule. Conforming decision, not an opportunity. Specification/rule-confirmation stage.
